title: add JSONSchema strict response_format with improved validation errors (OpenAI compatibility)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: make structured output via JSON Schema first-class and compatible with OpenAI-style response_format semantics. This PR introduces a strict mode for JSON Schema response_format that validates model output at emit time and surface precise error diagnostics to callers. It also harmonizes behavior with the OpenAI compatibility layer (function/tool calling and streaming) so existing customers can opt into stricter validation without surprising regressions. Summary of changes: 1) new response_format.strict boolean flag (default: false) and improved response_format.json_schema handling in the API layer; 2) streaming validation: per-chunk parsing/partial-validation with graceful backpressure and final-pass strict validation that fails the request with structured error payload when strict=true; 3) richer validation error model surfaced to clients (error_code, path, expected, actual, suggestion, snippet) and mapping to OpenAI-style error fields for compat; 4) safeguards and fallbacks: when a strict validation failure occurs, platform attempts auto-repair heuristics once (trim/trailing-comma fixes, attempt to parse concatenated JSON segments) before returning an error; 5) tests + docs + example upgrades. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged (strict=false). When a caller sets response_format.strict=true, we will validate and return HTTP 400 with application/json body containing structured error details matching Redwood error schema and carrying an openai_compat.errors array. See release notes and migration notes in docs. Checklist: - [x] core validation runtime implementation - [x] OpenAI compatibility layer mapping - [x] streaming integration and backpressure tests - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and examples - [x] changelog and migration notes - [x] e2e canary on staging for 48h Implementation notes: the validation is implemented in core/inference/response_format.go (lightweight streaming validator using incremental JSON tokenizer + schema-driven expectations), compatibility adapters in api/openai_compat/response_format_handler.go, and error canonicalization in pkg/observability/errors.go. Tests added under tests/integration/test_jsonschema_strict.py and tests/unit/test_jsonschema_partial_stream.py. The PR includes example client usage in examples/structured_output/openai_strict_mode.md. Performance: the incremental validator adds ~2-4% CPU for typical chat requests in strict mode; we added telemetry around validation latency and validation-induced rejections. Migration: customers can opt-in per-route via route.response_format.strict or per-request with the response_format flag. When strict=true and the model output cannot be validated, the API returns a structured error and an optional best-effort "raw_output" field for debug purposes (configurable via route settings).

release_notes: Add response_format.strict for JSON Schema structured output. When strict=true the platform validates model output and returns structured error details on validation failures. Defaults to false to preserve backwards compatibility. See docs/api/structured_output.md for migration and examples.
notes_for_support: Support: when customers report validation failures, ask for route config (response_format.strict and max_validation_buffer), full error payload (RWF_* codes), and optionally raw_output if available. Recommend setting auto_repair=false in regulated environments.
migration_instructions: To opt in: set route.response_format.strict = true in route config or add response_format: {"type":"json_schema","schema":<schema>,"strict":true} to the request. Monitor validation.rejections and validation.latency_ms metrics. If you rely on loose parsing, keep strict=false.
